subject: Urban Planning
title: Form-Based Codes: Regulating Shape, Not Use
description: A short lesson to help you apply Form-Based Codes: Regulating Shape, Not Use.

hook.text: Form-based codes don't care if a building is a home or a café. They care about its height, setback, and street relationship.

buildup.text: Traditional zoning asks 'what happens inside?' Form-based codes ask 'how does the building meet the sidewalk?'

discovery.text: Miami's form-based code lets any use in a building that fits the district's physical form. Permitting is faster.

twist.text: Developers love form-based codes because they reduce uncertainty. Neighbors like them because buildings fit the context.

climax.text: Over 600 US jurisdictions have adopted form-based codes. The shift from use to form is reshaping planning.

punchline.text: Don't regulate what's inside. Regulate how it looks from the street.

quiz.question: How do form-based codes differ from traditional zoning?
options: They regulate building shape and street relationship instead of use
They allow taller buildings in exchange for affordable housing
They require all buildings to match one architectural style
